title: Help people spot unusual PCB regions and understand the model’s decision.
purpose: I built this project to test whether a reference built from normal PCB images could help someone inspect an unfamiliar-looking region. Each experiment asks what improves detection, what causes mistakes and where an inspector still needs to make the judgment.

inspiration.title: Inspired by Seagate’s Project Athena
inspiration.text: Seagate’s 2019 Project Athena case study describes microscope-image inspection at its Normandale facility, where wafers are made for HDD read/write heads. The system flags anomalous images for an expert to assess. That workflow prompted my question: could a visual anomaly model give a reviewer useful evidence on a PCB?
inspiration.boundary: This independent educational project uses public VisA PCB photographs. I use no Seagate data or internal technology. My detector does not reproduce Athena or demonstrate performance in manufacturing.

why_one_class: I used normal images to build a reference, so the detector can measure unusual appearance without learning a classifier for every defect label. The small PatchCore-inspired model runs on a CPU and lets me inspect its scores, reference patches and mistakes.

principles.title: Keep the reviewer in the loop
principles.text: Show the original image beside the response, score and pose decision. A low score can still miss a real defect.

principles.title: Give each change a reason
principles.text: Test geometry, memory selection and orientation in separate steps. Keep the controls fixed and report any detections lost along the way.

principles.title: Know when to stop tuning
principles.text: Stage 6A examined the remaining misses. It did not support one clear next change, so I froze v1.0.

future.title: Test an untouched category
future.reason: PCB2 became development data after the first confirmation.
future.experiment: Declare the recipe and thresholds before testing a new category. Group observations by physical board when identifiers are available.
future.success: Report detection, localization, false alarms, uncertainty and failures together.

future.title: Improve small and missing-defect detection
future.reason: Six of the nine misses are canonical missing-label cases. Eight are small cases; these groups overlap.
future.experiment: In a new version, compare higher-detail or multi-scale features with normal-only calibration and controls matched for compute.
future.success: Increase small-defect recall while reporting any cost in false alarms or localization.

future.title: Test orientation on more examples
future.reason: I had only five reversed anomalies and no reversed normal controls.
future.experiment: Collect independent reversed normals and varied capture poses. Compare registration methods and keep explicit handling for uncertain poses.
future.success: Measure errors for each supported pose and check that correction preserves the defect signal.

future.title: Track individual defects and boards
future.reason: Union masks can combine defect labels, and the available data does not fully identify physical boards.
future.experiment: Obtain instance-level masks and board identifiers, then evaluate localization and generalization across boards.
future.success: Separate missing components from overlapping labels and account for related observations.

future.title: Test the reviewer’s workflow
future.reason: A benchmark cannot tell me whether the tool helps an inspector in a factory.
future.experiment: With appropriate real-world data, study reviewer decisions, capture variation, latency, drift and threshold policy.
future.success: Measure review outcomes and operational costs before claiming that the model is ready for deployment.

methods.title: Fit on normal images
methods.text: I use the official VisA one-class split. Normal fitting images build the reference memory, and held-out normals set the thresholds. Anomalies are used for evaluation. Once I used a test category to guide later changes, I labelled that work as development.
methods.reason: Keep defect labels out of fitting and threshold calibration, and show when evaluation data has influenced a decision.

methods.title: Preserve shape and check orientation
methods.text: The inherited colour and morphology rules locate the board. I apply fixed margins and letterbox the crop to 512 × 512. An RGB cue from the exterior pins identifies confidently reversed boards; only those crops are rotated exactly 180°. Uncertain crops stay unchanged.
methods.reason: Preserve board shape and local detail. Limit pose correction to the orientation that the evidence supports.

methods.title: Extract frozen patch features
methods.text: ResNet18 uses the frozen IMAGENET1K_V1 weights. I average layer2 and layer3 features over a 3 × 3 neighbourhood, align their grids and join them into 384-dimensional patch features.
methods.reason: Reuse pretrained visual features in a small CPU model without training a network to classify defects.

methods.title: Choose a normal reference bank
methods.text: The ordered D2 bank contains 4,096 float32 patches. I built it with projected approximate-greedy selection. At inference, each patch gets its exact Euclidean distance to the closest reference in the full 384-dimensional space.
methods.reason: Cover normal appearance within a fixed memory budget. The projection helps select references; it does not approximate the inference score.

methods.title: Score the image and map the response
methods.text: The image score is the largest native patch distance, including padding patches. I interpolate the map, remove the padding and return it to the original image coordinates, undoing the pose correction where needed. A result is flagged only when it is strictly greater than the frozen threshold.
methods.reason: Keep the decision rule reproducible. Map colours show response strength, not defect probability or exact defect boundaries.

methods.title: Check detection and localization separately
methods.text: I report image AP, AUROC, recall and normal false alarms, alongside pooled common-256 pixel AP/IoU and per-image diagnostics in common and source coordinates. I also examine pose groups and failures. PCB1 development, fresh PCB2 confirmation and later PCB2 development remain separate phases.
methods.reason: A model can detect an anomalous image while locating the defect poorly. Separate phases also prevent development results from being mistaken for a fresh test.

methods.title: Freeze the recipe and check it again
methods.text: SHA-256 records bind the scientific code, ordered bank, weights, thresholds, metrics and limitations. Six representative cases check scores, flags, poses and native/common/source maps against the saved Stage 5C outputs.
methods.reason: Make interface changes without changing the detector or recalibrating its decisions.

tools.name: Python 3.11 · PyTorch · Torchvision
tools.use: Extract frozen ResNet18 features, aggregate tensors and compute exact Euclidean scores in chunks on the CPU.
tools.reason: The project’s small implementation makes the scoring steps and normal references easy to inspect.

tools.name: NumPy · Pillow · SciPy
tools.use: Store banks and maps; decode bounded uploads, handle EXIF orientation, resize images and apply morphology and geometry rules.
tools.reason: Keep image coordinates and array transformations explicit while preserving the original geometry rules.

tools.name: pandas · scikit-learn
tools.use: Build diagnostic tables, summarize pose and defect groups, and calculate AP/AUROC.
tools.reason: Trace aggregate results back to individual cases and separate ranking quality from threshold decisions.

tools.name: Jupyter · Matplotlib
tools.use: Read saved artifacts and create contact sheets, distributions and before/after figures.
tools.reason: Inspect visual failures and compare the evidence behind each change.

tools.name: React · esbuild
tools.use: Manage inspection states and pages, then bundle the local and static interfaces.
tools.reason: Use the same workbench for live local inference and the labelled public evidence preview.

tools.name: Framer Motion · GSAP
tools.use: Framer Motion handles controls and result changes. GSAP ScrollTrigger tracks journey progress; ScrollToPlugin moves to a chosen stage.
tools.reason: Help readers follow state changes and navigate the journey, with keyboard focus, reduced motion and cleanup on route changes.

tools.name: Python standard-library HTTP · Vercel-ready static build
tools.versions: Local loopback server; separate public-preview build
tools.use: Run exact inference locally. The static build publishes evidence and recorded benchmark results without the model bank or weights.
tools.reason: Prepare a free portfolio deployment while clearly identifying which results are saved and where live inference runs.

tools.name: pytest · Playwright · Git · SHA-256
tools.versions: Pinned Python and npm locks; scientific recipe commit recorded in the model receipt
tools.use: Check regressions and browser flows, preserve project history and verify file identities.
tools.reason: Catch changed behaviour, retain known failures and trace displayed results to their scientific sources.
